## 裁决 — triage's grade and its fence

Triage seat, 2026-08-24 (finding concentration round, maintainer-invoked), promoted → `pm:queue` / Task. Verbatim:

> Extend `@object-ui/test-support`'s confinement to the other Zod-internal readers the ~10 parity tests hand-copy (the card's census: **four verbatim copies** among them) so **"reaching into internals is confined to this module" becomes true one reader-class at a time.** Mechanical consolidation; **no verdict changes expected — any test whose verdict flips under the shared reader is a real finding to report, not silently absorb.**

**That last clause is the whole card.** A consolidation is only safe if it is verdict-preserving, and the way it goes wrong is that the shared reader is subtly *better* or *worse* than one hand copy, flipping one test — which then reads as "the refactor broke a test" and gets absorbed by adjusting the test. ⛔ **Do not adjust a test to keep it green under the shared reader.** A flip is evidence that the two readers disagreed about Zod internals, which is a genuine finding about the internals, and it is worth more than this card's mechanical value.

**"One reader-class at a time" is scope, not style.** ⛔ Do not attempt every internals-reading pattern in one PR. Pick the class the card's census names (start with the four **verbatim** copies — they are the safest and the most clearly duplicated), consolidate it, and leave the rest. Say in the report which classes you did not take and why.

## PM mechanism assumptions — measure, do not assume

1. **"~10 parity tests" and "four verbatim" are the card's census from 2026-08-23.** Re-derive both on your merge-base and report the delta. ⚠️ `packages/types` has moved repeatedly today (#5981, #6003, #6012, and #6032 imminently), and #6032 in particular **rewrote part of `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`** — a file that is plausibly in your census. ⛔ Do not work from the card's list.
2. ⚠️ **"Verbatim" is a claim to verify byte-for-byte, not by eye.** Two copies that differ by a single `?.` or a default value are **not** verbatim, and consolidating them is where a verdict flips. Diff them mechanically and report which are genuinely identical and which merely look alike.
3. **The confinement claim is falsifiable — falsify it.** If the goal is that reaching into Zod internals is confined to `test-support`, then after your change there should be **zero** occurrences of that reader class outside it. ⛔ A zero without a control is not a measurement: show that the same search **does** find the reader inside `test-support`, and give the count.
4. **A shared reader is a new dependency edge.** Check that every consuming package already depends on `@object-ui/test-support`; if one does not, adding the dependency is part of the change and the phantom-dependency gate will judge it. ⛔ Do not add a workspace dependency silently.

## Verification

**The verdict-preservation claim is the deliverable and it must be measured, not asserted.** Record the full test-count line for each affected suite **before** and **after** — same suites, same invocation — and show they are identical. ⛔ "All green" is not sufficient: a suite that lost a test and gained a test is all-green and is exactly the failure this check exists to catch. Report file counts *and* test counts.

Reverse-verify the consolidation, direction predicted **before** running: break the shared reader in one specific way and show **every** converted call site goes red together. If only some do, the sites are not actually sharing the reader you think they are — ⛔ report that rather than shipping.

Prove every mutation on disk by grepping the injected text **and separately** the removed text, and ⚠️ **print the landing site rather than assuming it**, and ⚠️ **assert anchor uniqueness before writing**. Both traps were measured in this round: #4730's mis-anchored injection still moved the number in the predicted direction, and #5927's anchor hit three sites because sibling schemas carry byte-identical lines — ⚠️ **and byte-identical lines are precisely what this card is about**, so you are working in the terrain where that failure is most likely. Restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM`; `git diff HEAD --stat` empty afterwards.

Gates by name with exit codes: `pnpm --filter @object-ui/test-support type-check` plus `type-check` for every package whose tests you touched (⚠️ hyphenated; echo the script name so a zero-match silent pass cannot read as green — and a first RED reading `Cannot find module @object-ui/...` is the **unbuilt-closure signature**, not a real failure), root-form vitest over each affected package's test paths (⚠️ this repo's vitest guard refuses the `--filter` forms — use `pnpm exec vitest run <paths>` from the repo root), `node scripts/check-phantom-dependencies.mjs`, and eslint on changed files with the merge-base delta stated. ⚠️ Plain `eslint .` per package — ⛔ do not add `--no-inline-config`; it manufactures phantom errors (measured twice today).

Run `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` rather than guessing; empty frontmatter is this repo's "releases nothing" declaration. Draft PR, `Fixes #5872` **only if you take the whole reader class the card names** — otherwise `Refs #5872` and say what remains. ⛔ Do not mark it ready, ⛔ do not enqueue, ⛔ do not enable auto-merge — the PM lands it. Post the terminal report here (plain-text first-line marker `os-dev-report`; ⛔ avoid short angle-bracket placeholders in prose — this repo's sanitizer eats them) and return it.
